Q: How can I make http/https POST requests manually? A:

wget may help you.

get:

wget http://example.com

post:

wget --post-data "username=Yarkee" http://example.com

Q: How can I confirm the subscription request HTTP from Amazon SNS? A:

Basically, for testing, I used the ngrok server to make requests to my Python Flask server and added the HTTPS delivery type subscription to the AWS SNS topic.

In this case, for subscription confirmation, it triggered the endpoint, and that endpoint holds the SubscribeURL value. You need to put that value in the confirm subscription. For more details use:

Creating a subscription to an Amazon SNS topic

Q: Calling FindWindowW("Progman", "Program Manager") always returns a null handle A:

There are three issues with your code:

  1. FindWindowW requires UTF-16 encoded wchar_t strings, but koffi maps str to a UTF-8 encoded char string. Use str16 or wchar_t instead.

  2. Most Windows APIs, including FindWindowW, use the stdcall calling convention, but koffi defaults to cdecl instead. You have to use stdcall explicitly.

  3. The return value of FindWindowW is an HWND, which is a pointer type. Pointers have different sizes depending on whether you are using a 32bit or 64bit system. An int is not large enough to hold a pointer on a 64bit system. Use uintptr or void* instead. You can use koffi.alias('HWND', 'void *') to make it cleaner. Whatever you decide to use, make sure you use the same type in your other win32 function declarations, such as SendMessageTimeoutW.

Try this:

const HWND = koffi.alias('HWND', 'void *');

const FindWindowW = user32.func("HWND __stdcall FindWindowW(str16 lpClassNmae, str16 lpWindowName)");
// or
const FindWindowW = user32.func("HWND __stdcall FindWindowW(const wchar_t *lpClassNmae, const wchar_t *lpWindowName)");

Q: Shell command to tar directory excluding certain files/folders A:

Possibly also use cat/xargs/echo to emulate the --exclude-from=file option as rsync:

eval tar -cvzf tarball.tgz  $(cat exclude.lst | xargs -i echo -n "--exclude='{}' ") *

eval and single quotes around {} are used for special names (containing spaces, for example). If your folders do not have special chars in the name, you can skip the eval and the single quotes.

Q: C, structs and pointers - why does this work? A:

Your question is very similar to the following question:

I drove through a busy intersection although the traffic light was showing red. Why was I able to reach the other end of the intersection safely? Why did no collision with another car occur?

The answer to both this question and your original question is the same: You were lucky. Under slightly different circumstances (for example if you had entered the intersection a second earlier or later, or if your structure had been assigned a slightly different memory address with a different initial value), you may have been less lucky.

If you and everyone else abides by the rules, you will live in a safe predictable world in which (at least conceptually) nothing can go wrong. However, if you start breaking the rules, for example by driving through red traffic lights or dereferencing pointers that do not necessarily point to valid memory, then it is likely that sooner or later, something will go wrong.
